assumptions: No explicit initial state was specified, so the first listed FSM state, `increase`, is used as the root initial state.

The continuous computation of slip ratio/slip error from wheel speed, vehicle speed, and PID output is treated as outside the discrete supervisor scope; `slp` is modeled as the supervisor input used by the specified transition guards.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: single-wheel ABS hydraulic regulator as a three-state FSM
transition guards split the slip-error space into four bands using `slp`

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init verifies the assumed initial leaf is increase and its valve/pump outputs are applied after the first dispatch cycle.
scenario_results.name: default_init_enters_increase_outputs

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes the increase->hold guard boundary: slp just above 0.01 must not fire, while slp exactly 0.01 must hold.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies increase transitions exactly to hold when slp <= 0.01 and hold neutralizes both valves.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_threshold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes hold->increase guard: slp equal to 0.01 must stay hold, but slp above 0.01 must transition to increase.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies hold transitions exactly to increase when slp > 0.01 and increase commands inlet pressure.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_threshold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes hold->decrease guard: slp equal to -0.01 must stay hold, but slp below -0.01 must transition to decrease.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies hold transitions exactly to decrease when slp < -0.01 and decrease releases pressure with pump speed 500.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_threshold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes decrease->hold guard: slp below -0.01 must not fire, while slp exactly -0.01 must return to hold.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies decrease transitions exactly to hold when slp >= -0.01 and hold neutralizes both valves and pump.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_threshold

evidence: DSL defines states increase, hold, decrease under ABSHydraulicRegulator.
DSL actions match NL: increase sets k1=1,k2=0,n=0; hold sets k1=0,k2=0,n=0; decrease sets k1=0,k2=1,n=500.
DSL guards match NL thresholds: slp <= 0.01, slp > 0.01, slp < -0.01, slp >= -0.01.
GroundingMap source_summary assumption: no explicit initial state was specified, so increase is used as the root initial state.
findings.summary: The discrete three-state hydraulic supervisor is largely faithful to the NL, including states, valve/pump outputs, and slip-error guard thresholds. The main fidelity limitation is that the initial state is assumed rather than specified by the NL.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics.n_states_leaf = 3 and action_count = 3.
inspect_model_to_json_summary.transition_count = 5, including one initial transition and four guarded state transitions.
GroundingMap marks wheel_speed, vehicle_speed, and pid_output as required variables.
DSL declares wheel_speed, vehicle_speed, and pid_output but does not use them in guards or actions.
findings.summary: Required FSM components are covered, but the PID/slip-computation components described in the NL are represented only as declarations or an external scalar input, not as modeled behavior.

evidence: NL: "Wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute the slip ratio, and the PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor".
DSL: guards read only slp.
design_diagnostics_summary includes W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for wheel_speed, vehicle_speed, and pid_output.
design_diagnostics_summary includes W_VARIABLE_DECLARED_NEVER_USED for wheel_speed, vehicle_speed, and pid_output.
design_diagnostics_summary includes W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for slp.
findings.summary: The NL says wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute slip ratio and that PID output drives the supervisor, but the DSL does not compute slip, does not implement PID behavior, and does not use pid_output.

evidence: GroundingMap source_summary assumption: continuous computation is treated as outside the discrete supervisor scope; slp is modeled as supervisor input.
DSL contains no PID state, PID arithmetic, slip-ratio computation, or vehicle/wheel-speed update logic.
Core discrete transition policy is nevertheless explicitly modeled with slp thresholds.
findings.summary: The model collapses the continuous/PID side into an externally supplied slp value. This is acceptable as a within-scope discrete-supervisor candidate because the NL states continuous dynamics remain in the plant, but it prevents the model from being a strong end-to-end ABS/PID reference.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary.inspect_summary.nl_external_input_vars lists slp.
DSL writes k1, k2, and n in every state but never reads them.
DSL declares wheel_speed, vehicle_speed, and pid_output but does not read or write them.
W_HIGH_VAR_TO_LEAF_RATIO reports 7 variables for 3 leaf states.
findings.summary: Input, internal, and output roles are not cleanly separated. slp behaves as an external input; k1, k2, and n are pure outputs; wheel_speed, vehicle_speed, and pid_output are declaration-only placeholders.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary advisory W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for wheel_speed includes suggested_fix kind delete.
NL explicitly mentions wheel speed and vehicle speed being used to compute slip ratio.
GroundingMap marks variable:wheel_speed and variable:vehicle_speed as required.
findings.summary: The diagnostic suggested fix to delete declaration-only variables such as wheel_speed would be unsafe if applied blindly, because those variables are grounded in the NL even though they are outside or under-modeled in the current discrete supervisor.

evidence: No blocking design diagnostics: design_diagnostics_summary.ok = true and blocking_count = 0.
Simulation passes 9 of 9 scenarios.
Core states, transitions, guards, and actions are present.
PID output and wheel/vehicle speed computation are not behaviorally modeled.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T2 within-scope candidate. The FSM supervisor itself is concrete and testable, but the unused PID/slip-computation declarations and externalization of slp cap it below a strong reviewed candidate.

evidence: GroundingMap source_summary says continuous computation is treated as outside the discrete supervisor scope.
GroundingMap still marks wheel_speed, vehicle_speed, and pid_output as required variables.
DSL declares these variables but does not use them.
findings.summary: The root cause is scope ambiguity: the loop treated plant/PID/slip computation as outside the discrete supervisor, while still carrying NL-grounded variables into the DSL as required declarations. This produced unused-variable diagnostics and partial component coverage rather than an integrated model.
